keyword: how close will artemis 2 get to the moon
claims: The Artemis II Orion spacecraft reached its closest approach to the Moon on April 6, 2026.
The closest approach came within approximately 4,067 miles (about 6,545 kilometers) of the lunar surface.
The close flyby occurred while the crew passed behind the far side of the Moon.
The close flyby marked the first human mission to view the far side of the Moon since 1972.
The Orion capsule made its closest approach at approximately 7 p.m. EDT on April 6, 2026.
The approach took place as the spacecraft looped around the far side of the Moon.
The approach led to a temporary 40-minute communication blackout with Earth.
While within 4,067 miles of the Moon, the crew reached their maximum distance from Earth of roughly 252,756 miles.
The crew's maximum distance from Earth of roughly 252,756 miles broke the all-time human spaceflight record.
The maneuver was part of a free-return trajectory using lunar gravity to bring the crew back to Earth.
The crew consisted of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
The crew conducted observations during the flyby.
The crew took thousands of photographs during the flyby
